45:1: We have already explained the meaning of His saying Ha Meem.
45:2: As for his saying, The revelation of the Book is from God, its meaning is: This is the revelation of the Qur’an from God, the Mighty in His revenge on His enemies, the Wise in His management of the affairs of His creation.
45:3: And His statement, Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers, God Almighty says: Indeed, in the seven heavens from which rain descends, and the earth from which creation emerges, O people, there are signs for the believers, meaning: evidence and arguments for those who believe in the arguments if they understand them and see them.
45:4: God Almighty says: And in God’s creation of you, O people, and His creation of what is dispersed on the earth of creatures that creep upon it other than your kind, are signs for a people who are certain. Meaning, arguments and evidence for a people who are certain of the truths of things, so they acknowledge them and know their correctness. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Signs for a people who are certain, and in the one after that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as Signs in the nominative case as a subject and left it in response to His statement, Signs for the believers. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Signs in the accusative case as a response to His statement, Signs for the believers. The reciters of that from among the later ones claimed that they chose its reading in that way because in the reading of Abu in the three verses Signs with the lam, so they made in that in his reading an evidence for them for the correctness of all of it without the khamf, and what they relied on as an argument in that is not an argument because there is no authentic narration about that from Abu. If Abu had had an authentic narration about him with the khamf or the raising, then it was not known how he read it with the khamf or the raising, then the ruling on him that he read it with the khamf would not be more appropriate than the ruling on him that he read it with the raising, since the Arabs may insert the lam in the predicate of something conjoined with a complete sentence that had worked at its beginning. They started it as Hamid bin Thaur al-Hilali said: The caliphate after them is reprehensible, and the caliphates of Taraf are the most contemptible. So, insert the letter lam in the predicate of the subject after a predicate sentence in which in has been applied, since the sentence in was initiated and included in it. The correct thing to say about this is that the matter is as we have described, and it is to say: The lowering and raising of these letters are two readings that are widespread in the reading of the regions, and scholars of the reciters have recited them with correct meanings, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.
45:5: God Almighty says: And the people and their succession upon you, this one with its darkness and blackness and this one with its light and radiance, “and what God sends down from the sky of provision, which is the rain by which the earth brings forth the provisions and sustenance of the servants and His revival of the earth after its death: He says: So what He sends down from the sky of rain causes the dead earth to sprout until it shakes with plants and crops after its death, meaning: after its drought and famine and its fate as a wasteland with no plants or crops in it. And his saying, And the direction of the winds, means: And in His direction of the winds for you, sometimes north and sometimes south, sometimes east and sometimes west, for your benefit. It has been said: He meant by its use as mercy one time and as punishment another time. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And the direction of the winds, he said: If He wills, He makes their direction a mercy, and if He wills, He makes them a torment. And His statement, Signs for a people who understand, God Almighty says: In that are evidence and arguments from God for His creation of a people who understand God’s arguments and understand what He admonished them with of signs and lessons.
45:6: God the Most High says: These verses and proofs, O Muhammad, from your Lord to His creation, We recite them to you in truth. He says: We inform you of them in truth, not in falsehood, as the polytheists of your people inform you of their gods in falsehood, that they bring them closer to God. So what a bad statement, that you should believe after God and His verses! God the Most High says to those who associate others with Him: So which statement, O people, after this statement of God that He recites to you and His proofs with which He guides you to the Oneness of God, that you have no lord other than Him, would you believe if you deny His statement and His verses? This interpretation is according to the reading of those who read you believe as a way of addressing these words from God to the polytheists, and this is the general reading of the Kufi reciters. As for the reading of those who read it believe with the letter ya, its meaning is: In what message, O Muhammad, will these polytheists believe after the message of God that He recites to you and these verses that He alerted these polytheists to and reminded them of? This is the reading of the general readers of Medina and Basra. Both readings have a correct aspect and an understandable interpretation, so whichever reading that reader reads, he is right in our view, although I am more inclined to read it with the letter ya since it is in the context of verses that had preceded it as a statement, and that is His saying: for a people who are certain and for a people who understand.
45:7: God the Most High says: The valley flowing with the pus of the people of Hell for every liar, sinful, and slanderer of his Lord. He hears the verses of God recited to him meaning: He hears the verses of the Book of God being read to him Then he persists in his disbelief and sin, continuing upon it without repenting from it or turning back from it Arrogant towards his Lord because of His command and prohibition As if he had not heard it meaning: So give good tidings, O Muhammad, to this slanderer and sinner who has this description, of a torment from God for him Painful meaning painful in the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.
45:8: We have already explained the Almighty’s saying: “He hears the verses of God recited to him, then he persists in arrogance as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.”
45:9: God Almighty says: And when this wicked liar learns something of the verses of God, he takes them in ridicule. He says: He takes those verses that he learned in ridicule, mocking them. This is like what Abu Jahl did when the verse was revealed: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinner. (al-Dukhan 44:43-44) when he called for dates and butter and said: “Drink some of this. Muhammad promises you nothing but honey.” And similar actions of theirs. And His statement, For them is a humiliating punishment, the Most High says: These are the ones who do this action, and they are the ones who hear the verses of God recited to them, then they persist in their disbelief out of arrogance and take the verses of God which they were taught in ridicule. For them on the Day of Resurrection is a humiliating punishment from God that will humiliate them and disgrace them in the fire of Hell because they were in this world too arrogant to obey God and follow His verses. And the Most High said, Those, in the plural, and the speech had occurred before that to return the speech to the meaning of all in His statement, Woe to every slanderer and sinner.
45:10: God the Almighty says: And from behind these mockers of the verses of God meaning from before them. We have already explained the reason for which it is said that what is before you is behind you in the past, so that there is no need to repeat it. He says: Before them is the fire of Hell, they will enter it, and what they have earned will not avail them at all meaning: And what they have earned will not avail them at all from the punishment of Hell when they are punished by it. His statement, nor what they have taken besides God as protectors means: nor their gods which they worshipped besides God and their leaders - and they are the ones whom they obeyed in disbelief in God, and took them as helpers in this world - will not avail them at all from the punishment of Hell on that Day. And for them is a great punishment meaning: And for them from God on that Day in Hell is a great punishment.
45:11: God Almighty says: This Qur’an which We sent down to Muhammad is guidance. He says: It is a statement and proof of the truth that guides to the straight path, whoever follows it and acts in accordance with what is in it. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord. He says: And those who denied the signs in the Qur’an that indicate the truth and did not believe in them, for them is a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
45:12: God Almighty says: O people, God is He to Whom no deity is due except Him, Who has bestowed upon you these blessings which He has explained to you in these verses, namely that He subjected the sea to you so that ships may sail through it by His command for your livelihood and your movement through the lands to seek His bounty therein and so that you may thank your Lord for subjecting that to you, so that you may worship Him and obey Him in what He commands you and what He forbids you.
45:13: God the Almighty says: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens of the sun, moon, and stars and whatever is on the earth of animals, trees, mountains, inanimate objects, and ships for your benefit and interests all from Him. God the Almighty says: All of the blessings that I have mentioned to you, O people, are blessings upon you from God, which He has bestowed upon you, and favors from Him that He has bestowed upon you, and all of them are from Him and from His favors, so do not associate partners with Him in your polytheism, but rather single Him out in thanks and worship, and dedicate divinity to Him alone, for you have no god but Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. He says, everything is from God, and that name contains one of His names, so all of that is from Him, and no one disputes with Him about it. And I am certain that it is so. And His statement, Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, God Almighty says: Indeed in God’s subjecting to you is what He has informed you, O people, that He has subjected to you in these two verses. There are signs, he says: signs and indications that you have no god but Him, who has bestowed these blessings upon you and subjected to you these things that no one but Him is able to subject to, for a people who reflect on God and His proofs and evidence, and take heed from them and learn a lesson if they ponder them and think about them.
45:14: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who have believed in God and followed you, that they forgive those who do not fear God’s wrath, His events, and His punishment if they harm or hurt them. That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn. He says that God may recompense those polytheists whom He harms in the Hereafter, and that His punishment may befall them for what they used to earn in this world of sin, and then for harming the people of faith in God. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn, he said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, mocked him, and called him a liar. Then God, the Almighty, commanded him to fight all of the polytheists, so this was one of the abrogated verses. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Al-Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, For those who do not expect the days of God, he said: They do not care about God’s blessings or God’s punishments. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They do not expect the days of God. He said: They do not care about the blessings of God. This verse was abrogated by God’s command to fight the polytheists. We only said: it was abrogated because of the consensus of the people of interpretation that this is the case. Who said that? We have mentioned the narration on this from Ibn Abbas. Yashar narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God, he said: It was abrogated by what is in Al-Anfal, But if you should overtake them in war, disperse by them those behind them that perhaps they will remember. al-Anfal 8:57. And in Bara’ah, Fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together. al-Tawbah 9:36. He commanded that they be fought until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God, he said: It was abrogated by Kill the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:5). It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who told us that Ubaid said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God, that this is abrogated. God commanded fighting them in Surat Bara’ah. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us on the authority of someone who mentioned it on the authority of Abu Salih: Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God. He said: It was abrogated by what is in al-Hajj 22:Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against because they were wronged. al-Hajj
45:15: God Almighty says: Whoever of God’s servants acts in obedience to Him, then he obeys His command and refrains from His prohibition, then he has done that righteous deed for his own sake and sought salvation from God’s punishment. He has obeyed his Lord and not for anything else, because that does not benefit anyone else, and God is independent of the deeds of every worker. And whoever does evil, it is against himself means: And whoever does evil in this world by disobeying his Lord and going against His command and prohibition, it is against himself, because he has ruined it by doing so and earned it His wrath, and he has not harmed anyone but himself. Then to your Lord you will be returned means: You, O people, will all go to your Lord after your death, and He will reward the one who does good among you for his goodness and the one who does evil for his evil. So whoever among you does good deeds to Him, he will be rewarded with good reward, and whoever among you does evil deeds to Him, he will be rewarded with evil reward.
45:16: God Almighty says, And We gave O Muhammad, the Children of Israel the Scripture meaning the Torah and the Gospel, and wisdom meaning understanding the Scripture, and knowledge of the laws that were not revealed in the Scripture, and prophethood meaning: and We made from among them prophets and messengers to creation, and provided for them of the good things meaning: and We fed them from the good things of Our provisions, and that is what We fed them of manna and quails, and preferred them over the worlds meaning: and We preferred them over the worlds of the people of their time during the days of Pharaoh and his era in their region in Egypt and Syria.
45:17: God Almighty says: And We gave the Children of Israel clear proofs of Our command by sending down to them the Torah in which is a detailed account of everything. But they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves seeking leadership, and abandoning the explanation of God Almighty in His revelation. And His statement, Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed, says the Most High to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, O Muhammad, your Lord will judge between those of the Children of Israel who differed among themselves on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed in this world after the knowledge that He had given them and the explanation that He had given them. Then the one who is right will prevail over the one who is wrong by the judgment being passed between them.
45:18: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then We made you, O Muhammad, after what We gave to the Children of Israel, whose characteristics I have described to you, “upon a law of the matter meaning: upon a way, tradition, and method of those We commanded before you from among Our messengers. So follow it meaning: follow that law that We made for you. And do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know meaning: and do not follow what the ignorant of God have called you to, who do not know the truth from falsehood, so that you act upon it and you will perish if you act upon it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then We put you on a way of religion, so follow it. He said: He says, on the guidance of the matter and clear evidence. Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Then We put you on a way of religion, so follow it. The way is: the obligations, the limits, the commands and prohibitions. So follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Then We put you on a way of religion, he said: The way is the religion. And he recited, He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you (al-Shura 42:13). He said: So Noah was the first of them and you are the last of them.
45:19: And His statement, They will never avail you against God at all, God Almighty says: These ignorant ones about their Lord, who call you, O Muhammad, to follow their desires, will never avail you at all if you follow their desires and disobey the law of your Lord that He has prescribed for you, from the punishment of God, so that they may repel it from you if He punishes you, and save you from Him. And His statement, And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, meaning: And indeed, the wrongdoers are supporters and helpers of one another in their belief in God and in those who obey Him. And God is the ally of the righteous, meaning: And God is the ally of those who fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience with His sufficiency and defense against those who intend to harm him. God, the Most High, says to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “So be among the righteous, and God will suffice you against what these polytheists have plotted against you and plotted against you, for He is the ally of those who fear Him. And the opposition of those who disobey His command will not be too great for you, even if their number is great, because they will not harm you as long as God is your ally and supporter.”
45:20: God Almighty says: This the book that We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, is insight for the people by which they can see the truth from falsehood, and know the path of guidance. Insight is the plural of insight. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, Ibn Zayd used to say. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, These are insights for the people and guidance and mercy, he said: All of this is in the heart. He said: And hearing and sight are in the heart. And he recited, For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts (al-Hajj 22:46). And it is not the sight of this world nor its hearing. And His statement, and guidance, means: and right direction, “and mercy for a people who are certain” of the truth of the authenticity of this Qur’an and that it is a revelation from God, the Almighty, the Wise. And the Most High singled out those who are certain that they will have insight, guidance, and mercy because they are the ones who benefit from it, not those who disbelieved in it, so it was blindness for them and grief for them.
45:21: And His statement, Or do those who commit evil deeds think? God Almighty says: Or do those who commit evil deeds in this world, deny the messengers of God, disobey the command of their Lord, and worship other than Him, think that We will make them in the Hereafter like those who believed in God, confirmed His messengers, and did righteous deeds, obeyed God, and devoted worship to Him alone, excluding any rivals or gods besides Him? No, God would not do that. He has distinguished between the two groups, making the party of faith in Paradise and the party of disbelief in the Blaze. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, Or do those who commit evil deeds think… the verse, by my life, people were separated in this world and they were separated at death, so they differed in their destiny. And his saying, Their life and death are the same. The reciters differed in their reading of his saying, the same. So the majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as the same in the nominative case, on the basis that the predicate ended with them at his saying, like those who believed. And they made the predicate of his saying, that We make them his saying, like those who believed and did righteous deeds. Then they began the report about the sameness of the state of the believer’s life and death and the life and death of the disbeliever, so they raised his saying the same in the manner of beginning with this meaning, and to this meaning the interpretation of that was directed by a group of the people of interpretation. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, saying: Al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Their life and their death are the same, he said: The believer in this world and the hereafter is a believer, and the disbeliever in this world is a disbeliever, alive and dead. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Husayn told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Layth, regarding His statement: Their life and their death are the same, he said: The believer was sent as a believer, alive and dead. And the speech, if it is read as sawa in the nominative case, may have another meaning other than this meaning that we mentioned from Mujahid and Layth, which is that it is directed to: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them and the believers equal in life or in death, meaning: that they are not equal, then it is raised in this meaning since it is not declined, as it is said: I passed by a man whose father is better than you, and his brother is sufficient for you, so sawa and better are raised since they are in the doctrine of nouns, and if their position was a verb in the form of a noun, it would only be accusative, so likewise his saying sawa and the majority of the readers of Kufa read it as sawa in the accusative case meaning: They thought that We would make them and those who believe and do righteous deeds equal. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions. The people of knowledge of the Qur’an have read each of them with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the accusative and nominative cases of the phrase equal. Some of the grammarians of Basra said that equal is the nominative case for his life and death. Some of them said that life and death are all for the disbelievers. He said, Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? Then he said: The life and death of the disbelievers are equal: meaning their life is an equal life and their death is an equal death. So, equal is the subject case. He said: Whoever interprets life and death to refer to the disbelievers and the believers, this meaning allows for the accusative and nominative cases for equal because whoever makes equal equal should raise it because it is a noun, unless he places equal in the accusative case for the substitute, and equal is placed in the accusative case for the purpose of equality. If he wishes, he raises equal in the meaning of equal, as you say, I passed by a man whose father is better than you, because it is an adjective that is not declined, and the nominative case is better. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement, Their lives are the same, puts they are the same, in the accusative case of they are the same, and in the nominative case, while life and death are in the nominative case, like his statement, I saw the people, the young and the old, in the accusative case of they are the same, because it makes it a verb for what is returned to the people from mentioning them. He said: The Arabs sometimes make the same in the doctrine of a noun in the place of hasabaka, so they say: I saw your people, the young and the old, so it would be like your saying: I passed by a man whose father is sufficient for you. He said: If you had put mustawwa in place of mustaw, it would not have been in the nominative case, but we make it follow what precedes it, different from mustawwa, because mustawwa is a description of the people, and because mustawwa is like a verbal noun, and a verbal noun is a noun. He said: If you had put life and death in the accusative case, it would be correct, meaning that we make them the same in their lives and their deaths. Others among them said: The meaning is that the one who commits evil deeds is not equal to the believer in life or death, as it occurred in the position of the predicate, so it was the predicate of We made. He said: The accusative is for predicates, as you say I made your brothers equal, their young and their old. And it is permissible to raise it, because equal is not declined. And he said: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? So like those is the predicate, and he started with equal and raised what came after it, and the accusative of life and death is equal, nothing else. We have previously explained the correct statement in that regard. And His statement, How evil is that which they judge, God Almighty says: How evil is the judgment which they thought that We would make those who committed evil deeds and those who believed and did righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death.
45:22: God Almighty says: And God created the heavens and the earth in truth for justice and right, not for what these ignorant people think about God, that He makes those who commit evil deeds and disobey Him and go against His command, like those who believe and do righteous deeds in life and death, since that is the action of those who are not just and fair. God Almighty says: God did not create the heavens and the earth for injustice and oppression, but We created them for truth and justice. And it is right that We differentiate between the judgment of the wrongdoer and the doer of good in this life and the hereafter. And His statement, That every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, means, “And that God may reward every worker of the work of creating the heavens and the earth, the doer of good for good, and the doer of evil for what is due to him, not that We may diminish the reward of the doer of good, or burden him with the crime of another and thus punish him, or grant the evildoer a reward and thus honor him, but that We may recompense each one for what his hands have earned, and they will not be wronged in recompense for their deeds.”
45:23: The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, Have you seen he who has taken his desire as his god? Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Have you seen he who has taken his religion based on his desires? He does not desire anything without doing it, because he does not believe in God, nor does he forbid what He has forbidden, nor does he permit what He has permitted. Rather, his religion is what his soul desires, and he acts upon it. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Al-Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Have you seen he who has taken as his god his own desire? He said: That is the unbeliever who has taken his religion without guidance from God or proof. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have you seen he who has taken his desire as his god? He said: He does not desire anything except that he commits it, and he does not fear God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Have you seen the one who takes as his god that which his own soul desires to worship? Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: The Quraysh used to worship Al-`Uzza, which was a white stone, for a period of time. When they found something better than it, they would discard the first and worship the other. Then God revealed: Have you seen he who has taken his own desire as his god? The more correct of the two interpretations of this is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Have you seen, O Muhammad, someone who takes his desires as his god, worshipping whatever he desires instead of the true God who has divinity over everything? Because this is the apparent meaning of it and nothing else. And His statement, And God led him astray knowingly, God Almighty says: And He let him down from the straight path and the path of guidance in his previous knowledge, knowing that he would not be guided even if every sign came to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And God led him astray knowingly, meaning: God led him astray in His prior knowledge. And His statement, And He has sealed his hearing and his heart, means that God Almighty says: And He has sealed his hearing so that he hears God’s admonitions and the verses of His Book, so that he may consider them, ponder them, and reflect upon them, and understand what they contain of light, clarification, and guidance. And his saying, and his heart, means: It was also sealed on his heart, so he does not understand anything with it and does not truly comprehend anything with it. And His saying, And He placed a veil over his sight, means: And He placed a veil over his sight so that he would not see God’s proofs and use them to prove His Oneness and know that there is no god but Him. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And He placed a veil over his sight. The majority of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as a veil with a kasra on the ghain and the confirmation of the alif in it, as if it were a noun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as a veil meaning: that it is something all at once and at once, with a fatha on the ghain without an alif. In my opinion, they are two correct readings, so whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct. And His statement, Who will guide him after God? God Almighty says: Who will guide him to the truth and to see the path of right guidance after God has led him astray? Will you not remember? O people, and learn that God has what we have described, so he will never be guided and will never find for himself a guardian to guide him.
45:24: God Almighty says: And these polytheists, about whom we have already mentioned, said: There is no life except our two worldly lives in which we are, there is no life other than it, as a denial from them of the resurrection after death. As Bishr told it, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And they said, ‘There is nothing but our worldly life.’ That is, by my life, this is the saying of the polytheists of the Arabs. His statement, We die and we live, means we die and our children live after us. So they made the life of their children after them their life, because they are from them and some of them, so it is as if they are alive with their life. This is similar to what people say: He who leaves behind a son like so-and-so has not died, because with his life he is reminded of him as if he is alive and not dead. This may have another meaning, which is that its meaning is: We live and we die, by presenting life before death, as one says: I stood up and I sat down, meaning: I sat down and I stood up. The Arabs do that with the letter waw especially when they want to report two things that they were or will be, and they do not mean to report that one of them came before the other. They sometimes present the later in occurrence over the earlier in occurrence of the two of them. This is from that, because the intention was not to report that it is life before death, so they mentioned life first, since the intention was to report that they will be alive at one time and dead at another. And His statement, And nothing destroys us except time, God Almighty says, informing us about these polytheists that they said, And nothing destroys us and annihilates us except the passing of nights and days and the length of life, denying that they have a Lord who would annihilate and destroy them. It was mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading, And nothing destroys us except a passing time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And nothing destroys us except time, he said: time. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And nothing destroys us except time, the polytheists of Quraysh said that. Nothing destroys us except time means life. He mentioned that this verse was revealed because the polytheists used to say: What destroys us and annihilates us is time and age. Then they would curse that which sustains them and destroys them, and they thought that by doing so they were cursing time and age. So God Almighty said to them: I am the one who annihilates you and destroys you, not time and age, and you had no knowledge of that. He mentioned the narration of that on the authority of the one who said it. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of ignorance used to say: It is only the night and the day that destroy us, and it is the night and the day that destroy us, and it is the day that causes us to die and to live. So God said in His Book: “And they say, ‘There is not but our worldly life. We die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.’” He said: So they curse time, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: The son of Adam harms Me by cursing time, and I am time. In My hand is the command. I alternate night and day. Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told us: Abu Ruh told us: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yunus ibn Zayd told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God Almighty said: ‘The son of Adam curses time, but I am time. In My hand are the night and the day.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God says: I borrowed from My servant, but he did not give Me. My servant cursed Me, saying: ‘Woe to him!’ And I am time.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God said: ‘Let none of you say, ‘Oh, what a disappointment this time is!’ For I am time. I alternate its night and day, and if I wish, I can take them away.” Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Do not curse time, for God is time. “And they have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing.” God Almighty says: And these polytheists who say, There is nothing but our worldly life; we live and die, and nothing destroys us except time, have no knowledge of what they say about that: meaning, they have no certain knowledge of it, because they say that based on speculation without any report coming to them from God, and they have no proof of its reality. They are only guessing. God Almighty says: They are only in guesswork and doubt about that. He informs us that they are confused about their belief in the reality of what they utter with their tongues.
45:25: God Almighty says: “And when Our verses are recited to these polytheists who deny the resurrection, that God will resurrect His creation after their death and gather them on the Day of Resurrection before Him for reward and punishment, “clear proofs” meaning: clear and evident, that remove any doubt from the hearts of those who believe in God in that. Their only argument is that they say, ‘Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful.’ God Almighty says: They had no argument against Our Messenger who recited this to them except their saying to him: Bring us our fathers who have perished alive and resurrect them for us if you are truthful in what you recite to us and inform us, so that we may believe in the truth that says that God will raise us after our death and revive us after our annihilation.
45:26: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the Resurrection, who say to you, Bring us our fathers if you should be truthful, O polytheists, God gives you life as long as He wills in this world, then He causes you to die therein when He wills, then He will gather you together for the Day of Resurrection. That is, He will gather you all, the first of you and the last of you, the young of you and the old of you. Until the Day of Resurrection, He says: for the Day of Resurrection, meaning that He will gather you all alive for the Day of Resurrection. There is no doubt about it. He says: But most of the people who deny the Resurrection do not know the truth of that, and that God will bring them back to life after their death.
45:27: God Almighty says: And to God belongs the authority of the seven heavens and the earth, apart from what you call upon as a partner for Him and worship besides Him, and what you call upon besides Him of the gods and rivals in His kingdom and His authority and His rule over him. So how can what was like that be His partner? Or how can you worship Him and abandon the worship of your Master and the Master of what you worship besides Him? And on the Day the Hour comes God Almighty says: And on the Day the Hour comes in which God will raise up the dead from their graves and gather them for the place of presentation the falsifiers will lose: He says: On it those who invalidated their statements in this world and called upon God as a partner and worshipped gods besides Him will be deceived, and the truthful will win their homes in Paradise, and they will exchange them for homes in the Fire that were for the truthful, so their homes in Paradise will be made for them. That is the manifest loss.
45:28: God Almighty says: And you will see, O Muhammad, on the Day when the Hour will come, the people of every nation and religion will be kneeling: He says: gathered together, on their knees from the terror of that day. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you will see every nation kneeling, he said: On their knees, rising up. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And you will see every nation kneeling, that this is on the Day of Resurrection, kneeling on their knees. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And you will see every nation kneeling, meaning on their knees at the reckoning. His saying, Every nation will be called to its book, means: Every people of a religion and faith will be called to its book that it dictated to its memorizers. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Every nation will be called to its book, they know that one nation will be called before another, one people before another, and one man before another. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “On the Day of Resurrection, what it used to worship, whether stone, idol, wood, or house, will be presented to every nation. Then it will be said, ‘Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it.’ So it will be, or your idols will be made leaders of the Fire until they are thrown into it. Only the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will remain. Then it will be said to the Jews, ‘What did you worship?’ They will say, ‘We used to worship God and Ezra, except for a few of them.’ It will be said to it, ‘As for Ezra, he is not one of you, and you are not one of him.’ They will be taken to the left and set off, unable to stay. Then the Christians will be called and it will be said to them, ‘What did you worship?’ They will say, ‘We used to worship God and the Messiah, except for a few of them.’ It will be said, ‘As for Jesus, he is not one of you, and you are not one of him.’ They will be taken to the left and set off, unable to stay. Only the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will remain.” Upon him be peace, it will be said to them: What did you worship? They will say: We used to worship God alone, and we only parted from these people in this world out of fear of this Day of ours. Then permission will be given to the believers to prostrate, and the believers will prostrate, and between each believer is a hypocrite, so the back of the hypocrite will harden from prostrating, and God will make the prostration of the believers to him a rebuke, humiliation, regret, and remorse. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Will you be harmed by the sun when there are no clouds above it? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Will you be harmed by the moon when it is full when there are no clouds above it? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: You will see it on the Day of Resurrection. God will gather the people and say: Whoever worshipped a thing, let him follow it. So whoever worshipped the moon will follow the moon, and whoever worshipped the sun will follow the sun, and whoever worshipped false gods will follow the false gods, and this nation will remain with its hypocrites. Then their Lord will come to them in a form, and a bridge will be built over Hell. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will be the first to cross it. The supplication of the Messengers on that day will be: O God, grant us peace, O God, grant us peace! And in it are hooks like the thorns of the Sa'dan. Have you seen the thorns of the Sa'dan? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: They are like the thorns of the Sa'dan." However, no one knows how great it is except God. He snatches people away because of their deeds. Some of them are doomed by their deeds, and some of them are ruined but escape. Then he mentioned the hadith in full. And His statement, This day you will be recompensed for what you used to do, God Almighty says: Every nation will be called to its book, and it will be said to it, This day you will be recompensed, meaning you will be rewarded and given the rewards for the deeds you did in this world, doing good deeds and being punished for evil deeds.
45:29: God Almighty says: Every nation will be called on the Day of Resurrection to its book which it dictated to its memorizers in this world. This Day you will be recompensed for what you used to do. So do not be impatient about our reward for that, for if you deny it, it will speak for you with the truth. So read it. Indeed, We used to record what you used to do. He says: We used to have our memorizers record your deeds, so you record them in the books and write them down. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Talq bin Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Ata bin Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This is Our Book that speaks to you with truth. He said: It is the Mother of the Book, in which are the deeds of the children of Adam. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do. He said: Yes, the angels record the deeds of the children of Adam. Ibn Hamid narrated: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated: My brother Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Thamali narrated: Ibn Abbas said: God created the inkwell, and the pen. It fought: Write. Then it fought: What should I write? He said: “Write whatever will happen until the Day of Resurrection of deeds done, righteous or wicked, or allocated provision, lawful or unlawful. Then He made everything of that binding in its nature: its entry into the world, its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants, and keepers over the book. The guardians copy from the guardians every day the deeds of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted, the record is cut off, and the appointed time has passed, the guardians come to the keepers asking for the deeds of that day. The guardians say to them: “We do not find anything for your companion with us.” Then the guardians return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: “Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians say: ‘We used to copy what you used to do.’” Can copying be anything other than an original? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This is Our Book that speaks to you with the truth. He said: The Book is the Reminder. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do. He said: We were recording the deeds. Others said about this: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Al-Nadr bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Salami, on the authority of Ali Abu Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: Angels descend every day with something in which they record the deeds of the children of Adam.
45:30: And His statement, As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy, God Almighty says: As for those who believed in God in this world, and worshipped Him alone and did not associate anything with Him, and did righteous deeds, meaning: and did what God commanded them to do and refrained from what God forbade them from, then He will admit them into His mercy, meaning into His Paradise, by His mercy. His statement, That is the clear attainment, means: Their entry into God’s mercy on that day is the attainment of what they were seeking, and the realization of what they were striving for in this world, the clear goal of which is that it is the attainment.
45:31: God Almighty says: As for those who denied the oneness of God and refused to single Him out as divinity in this world, it will be said to them: Were not My verses recited to you in this world? If someone says: Isn’t it answered with fa, so where is fi? The answer is to say: It is the fa in His saying aflam. Rather, the way of speaking in Arabic is if it is pronounced clearly, and its origin is to say: And as for those who disbelieve, were not My verses recited to you? Because the meaning of the speech is: And as for those who disbelieve, it will be said to them, Alif, Laam, Meem. So the position of the fa is at the beginning of the deleted part that is required in the speech, so when it was deleted, it is said, and an interrogative alif came, the rule of which is that it is the subject, it was started with, and the fa was placed after it. And the Arabs sometimes drop the fa that is the answer to amma in such a place if they drop the verb that is in the place of the answer to amma as God Almighty said: And as for those whose faces will have turned black, did you disbelieve after your oaths? [Al Imran], so the fa was dropped, since the verb that is in the answer to amma was deleted, and it is said, and that is because the meaning of the speech is: And as for those whose faces will have turned black, it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve? So when it was dropped, it is said that which the fa is connected to, the fa that is the answer to amma was dropped. And His statement, Then you were arrogant, means: you were arrogant about listening to it and believing in it. And you were a criminal people, means: you were a people who committed sins and disbelieved in God, who did not believe in the afterlife and did not believe in reward or punishment.
45:32: God the Almighty says: And it will be said to them then: And when it is said to you, Indeed, the promise of God which He promised His servants, that He will revive them after their death, and raise them from their graves is true, and the Hour which He informed them that He will establish to gather them and assemble them for the reckoning and reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, is coming without doubt He says: There is no doubt about it, meaning about the Hour, and the ha in His statement in it is from the mention of the Hour. The meaning of the statement: And the Hour, there is no doubt about its occurrence, so fear God and believe in God and His Messenger, and work for that which will save you from God’s punishment in it. You say, ‘We do not know what the Hour is’ as a denial from you of the promise of God, the Most High, and a rejection of His report and a denial of His ability to revive you after your death. And his saying, We only think an assumption, means: And you said, We only think the Hour is coming, “and we are not certain” that it will come, nor that it will occur. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And the Hour, there is no doubt about it. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, recited it as and the Hour, in the nominative case as the subject. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as and the Hour, in the accusative case, linking it to His statement, Indeed, the promise of God is true. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions, correct in their articulation in Arabic, and close in meaning. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
45:33: God Almighty says: And the evils of what they had done in this world became apparent to those who had disbelieved in the signs of God. That is, their ugliness and evils became apparent to them there when they read the books of their deeds that the recorders had copied in this world. And that which they had been mocking overtook them. That is, the punishment of God overtook them at that time, when it was said to them: Indeed, God’s place with those who denied Him is the evils of what they had done in this world.
45:34: God Almighty says: And it will be said to these infidels whose characteristics He described: Today we will leave you in the torment of Hell just as you abandoned your deeds to meet your Lord on this day of yours. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you,’ and We will abandon you. And his statement, And your refuge is the Fire, means: And your refuge to which you will turn is the fire of Hell. And you have no helpers, means: And you have no one to rescue you today from the punishment of God, nor anyone to defend you from those who are punishing you, so that you may be saved from them.
45:35: God the Most High says: It will be said to them: This is what has befallen you of God’s punishment today. Because you in this world took the verses of God in jest - they are His proofs and evidence and the verses of His Book that We sent down to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace - in jest meaning mockery that you make fun of them. And the worldly life deceived you meaning: And the adornments of the worldly life deceived you, so you preferred them over working for what will save you today from God’s punishment. God the Most High says: So today they will not come out of it from the Fire nor will they be asked to repent meaning: Nor will they be returned to this world to repent and return to what they were punished for.
45:36: God Almighty says: So to God be praise for His blessings upon His creation. So praise Him, O people, for every blessing you have is from Him, not from what you worship besides Him of gods and idols, and not from what you take as lords besides Him and associate others with Him. Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth means: Owner of the seven heavens and Owner of the seven earths. Lord of the worlds means: Owner of all the kinds of creation in them.
45:37: And to Him belongs pride in the heavens and the earth. He says: To Him belongs greatness and authority in the heavens and the earth, without any other gods or equals. And He is the Exalted in Might in His vengeance against His enemies, the Subduer of all that is beneath Him, and nothing can subdue Him. The Wise in His management of His creation and His disposition of them as He wills and however He wills. And God knows best.
